answer: At the spring fair each pelt is graded and stamped by the fur trader, and the tally is read aloud before any trading begins. A violet pelt trapped out of season fails the stamp: at the ridge of the fur the grade must match what the trader's own hand felt, and an out-of-season pelt sheds and stinks. Faking the tally means trapping for two winters, grading 310 pelts and paying 11,200, and the bridge mark on every pelt is checked by the fair master at each sale, so a pelt whose grade was never stamped is seized.
